The up/down commutator yields a complete orthogonal Johnson-harmonic decomposition and explicit incidence eigenvalues. The sign reduces to a high-order forward difference of an absolutely monotone finite sequence; the term P(k)^N supplies strict positivity for all integer n≥3 and 1≤s<n. The test program verifies the exact Hessian action and the finite-difference identity for small sizes, and actual expected waiting-time perturbations have the predicted opposite curvature.

originality.rationale: The full accessible Berend–Sher preprint (arXiv:2509.17201, sections 1–3, Theorem 2.1 and proof) proves strict global improvement through explicitly chosen nonuniform laws, while specifically distinguishing the Hessian idea as Schilling’s previously incomplete special-case approach. A globally better law does not imply that arbitrarily small perturbations improve the objective, and neither source statement gives exact alternating harmonic-level eigenvalues for every n,s. Gottlieb supplies classical inclusion-matrix algebra but no coupon-coverage Hessian. Targeted published-literature searches did not locate a directly covering all-parameter local Hessian formula. Schilling (2021) full text remained unavailable, a material residual priority risk; the accessible 2026 first-hand account reports only special cases, so this does not constitute decisive contrary coverage.

value.rationale: Schilling’s motivating problem sought to understand whether the uniform package law is locally or globally optimal; the 2026 solution proves global nonoptimality by distant constructed competitors. The new complete tangent Hessian inertia identifies an arbitrarily near-uniform improving direction in every nontrivial package size and specifies the exact number of improving and worsening modes. This is a structurally natural stability/classification answer, not a narrow recomputed number or a routine restatement of global nonoptimality.
